newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-LINDH WINS WOMEN'S DOWNHILL GOLD.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-LINDH WINS WOMEN'S DOWNHILL GOLD.

text.p: Hilary Lindh of the United States won the women's downhill gold medal at the Alpine skiing world championships on Saturday, stunning the pre-race favourites and continuing a north American tradition.
Lindh, who has not finished in the top three of any World Cup race this season, clocked one minute 41.18 seconds in brilliant sunshine on the Kandahar-Banchetta piste.

Switzerland's Heidi Zurbriggen took the silver medal in 1:41.24 and Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg, a double world champion at the last championships in 1996 but without a medal in Sestriere before Saturday, was delighted with the bronze in 1:41.44.
Italy's Isolde Kostner, winner of the super-G earlier in the week, finished fourth.

Lindh, the 1992 Olympic downhill silver medallist who last won a race in 1994, followed in the wake of 1996 downhill champion and compatriot Picabo Street -- who is absent this year due to injury -- and 1993 champion Kate Pace of Canada.
The last European to win the women's downhill title was Austrian Petra Kronberger in Saalbach in 1991.

"I thought maybe I could win a medal but I didn't know I could be first," said the 27-year-old Lindh, who won a bronze in the discipline last year in Sierra Nevada although she had not been on the podium all season before that race either.
"I guess when I race big events I get excited," she said.
